1. (Judgment 1) Tonight reads as a rerun of 2026-11-09 "Designed and shipped by the same hands.": the same claim in other words, the same artifact-led Spaceman plate, and an olive-brass ground. The structural silhouette also nearly matches 2026-11-15: irregular-twelve, broken, full-bleed, dense, syncopated, drenched, reorder, outline caps. Push the composition and the caption away from both nights, for example by making the client ledger the visual carrier instead of another engraved-plate statement about one person doing both jobs.
2. (Judgment 6) `nav_form: word` is not executed. At 1440, Work / About / Contact sit permanently visible under "Index," and at 360 they sit in the top bar, so the page shows a label row plus a heading. Show only the small-caps word "Index" until it is activated. On the phone, move the links into the footer data strip as `nav_360` declares.
3. (Judgment 2) In the client ledger at 360, several logos do not read. LastPass renders as "L st a" because its letterforms drop out against the olive. Sapient Razorfish is clipped to a stray "s" over "sapien." Rolex is too small to read. Give the dark-ink logos a light knockout or plate, or drop the logo column where it cannot carry, so the ledger never looks like a broken image.
4. (Judgment 5) The deck says Spaceman means "no files handed between teams, one pair of hands." The record says the work is done "sometimes as a solo contributor, sometimes embedded in a larger team." Rewrite the sentence so it does not claim he always works alone.
5. (Judgment 5) The plate label reads "LLC · EST. 2018 · ALDIE, VIRGINIA." No location for Spaceman appears in the work records; Aldie comes from the weather signal. Remove the location from the Spaceman metadata, or keep it only in the signal strip.

1. Freshness: this reads as a rerun of 2026-11-09, "a maker's spec plate: one project reversed out of an olive…". That night was also an olive-brass artifact plate built around one owned project. Its hero "Designed and shipped by the same hands." makes the same claim as tonight's "Design and build on the same desk.", which also echoes 10-31 "Design and engineering as one job, not two teams passing files." Change at least two of these three: the hero phrase's claim, the olive-brass hue family, or the spec-plate framing. A returning visitor should not take tonight for 11-09 in a new font.

2. Legibility: in the 360 client ledger, the LastPass tile renders as "L st a" with glyphs missing. The Sapient Razorfish tile shows a stray "s" floating over "sapien" with the rest of the logo gone. Both read as broken images in the evidence column. Fix the SVGs, or set those two clients as tracked-caps names like the Zeldman tile.

3. Hierarchy: the brief puts SPACEMAN across cols 1–9 with the metadata title-block in cols 10–12 beside it, reading left to right. At 1440, SPACEMAN stops around col 6, and the YEAR/ROLE/SCOPE/CLIENTS block sits below the deck rather than right of the nameplate. Widen SPACEMAN to the declared span and move the title-block up so it runs beside the plate. The thesis-left / evidence-right split should be visible in the first fold.

1. Freshness: this reads as a rerun of 2026-11-09, "a maker's spec plate: one project reversed out of an olive…". That night was also olive brass and also an artifact plate. Keep the SPACEMAN nameplate, but caption it with a phrase that makes a claim no recent night made, such as the roster or the ten years. Rewrite the standfirst so it does not echo 10-31.

2. Hierarchy (Type Treatment `weight: heavy`): SPACEMAN is a hairline outline of a light-to-regular cut. At 1440 it reads lighter than the solid caption beneath it, which works against the declared heavy direction and against the artifact leading. Outline the heavy (800–900) cut of Big Shoulders and thicken the stroke so the engraved channels carry real weight.

Restore the size differential so SPACEMAN visibly dominates.

Add vertical padding or increase line-height on these nav/link rows site-wide.
